chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “May I be your ransom, who washed Fāṭimah عليها السلام?” He said, “That was Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام.” He said: It was as though I regarded that as something immense from his statement. He said, “It is as though you felt constrained by what I informed you of.” I said, “Indeed that was so, may I be your ransom.” He said, “Do not feel constrained, for she was a ṣiddīqah; none but a ṣiddīq would wash her. Do you not know that Maryam عليها السلام was washed by none but ʿĪsā عليه السلام?”

He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who is on a journey with men among whom there is no maḥram for her, and there is no woman with them, then the woman dies—what is to be done with her?” He said, “Of her, that which Allah has made subject to tayammum is to be washed, and she is not to be touched, and nothing of her beauties that Allah has commanded to be concealed is to be uncovered.”
So I said, “Then how is that to be done with her?” He said, “The inner sides of her palms are washed, then her face is washed.”

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: dry ablution used here as the legal basis for limited washing without full contact
key_terms.بَطْنُ كَفَّيْهَا: the inner sides of her palms
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden
key_terms.صِدِّيقٌ: a supremely truthful and righteous person fit for a sacred duty
key_terms.صِدِّيقَةٌ: a supremely truthful and righteous woman of exceptional spiritual rank
key_terms.غَسَّلَ: performed the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.مَحَاسِنِهَا: the parts of her beauty and body that must remain covered

ai.seo_question: Who washed Fāṭimah عليها السلام, and what is the ruling when a woman dies while traveling with unrelated men and no other woman is present?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام washed Fāṭimah عليها السلام and presents this as fitting for her rank as a ṣiddīqah. It also gives a legal ruling for the case of a deceased woman traveling among unrelated men, instructing that only limited washing be performed without touch or uncovering what Allah has commanded to be concealed.
